incidents.name: Hector redemption TokenVault eligible-wallet drain
incidents.notes: The TokenVault's onlyModerator addEligibleWallet() was used by Hector's own deployer/moderator EOA to credit the attacker with the full redemption amount, after which the permissionless mintWithdraw() legitimately paid 2,788,764.90 USDC out of the HectorRedemptionTreasury - a centralization/key-control failure that CertiK had already flagged as an acknowledged risk, not a defeat of the contract logic.

sources.ref: onchain review: TokenVault 0x0a5053bff7e5a763b91fbd60ad1b04edc64cb803 created 2024-01-09 by 0x55add83fba10b9b6065f9599817d3a2540ad4ffe; that same moderator EOA called addEligibleWallet at block 19010121, 232 blocks before the attacker 0x86d3e3e133e32c1f2afe8069163a19da01a5ef7c called mintWithdraw at block 19010353, and repeated it for a second drain wallet at block 19010462; exploit tx moves exactly 2,788,764.900936 USDC from treasury 0x8b0870867d4c8519f0a56381e74b0217c039401c. CertiK classifies the cause as centralization risk / private-key leak / inside job.
